approach: Show the learner the Spanish already around them in the US (who speaks it, where it appears on signs, in place names and in media) so they notice and read it every day.
coverage: About 43 million people in the US speak Spanish at home (Census, 2023)
Counting second-language speakers, estimates reach roughly 55 to 60 million
The US Hispanic population is about 65 million; not every Hispanic person speaks Spanish
Most US Hispanics are of Mexican origin; Puerto Rican, Salvadoran, Cuban and Dominican roots are next
Signs: Salida, Entrada, Empuje, Jale, Cuidado: piso mojado, Baños, Se habla español
Place names: Los Ángeles, Las Vegas, Florida, Nevada, Colorado, Montana, El Paso

blocks.purpose: Gives the real numbers behind "Spanish in the US", carefully worded.

paragraphs: The United States is one of the largest Spanish-speaking countries in the world. About 43 million people here speak Spanish at home, according to the Census Bureau's 2023 survey. Counting people who speak it as a second language, estimates come close to 60 million.

About 65 million people in the US are Hispanic or Latino. Not all of them speak Spanish, and many Spanish speakers are not Hispanic. Most Hispanic Americans have roots in Mexico; Puerto Rican, Salvadoran, Cuban and Dominican roots are the next largest groups.

sections.heading: Where to notice it
paragraphs: On TV and radio: Univision and Telemundo are the largest Spanish-language networks in the US. On products: read the Spanish side of bilingual labels, such as Instrucciones (instructions), Ingredientes (ingredients) and Hecho en México (made in Mexico). Between neighbors: listen for ¡Buenos días!, ¿Qué tal? (How is it going?) and ¡Nos vemos! (See you!).

blocks.purpose: Targets the assumption that every Hispanic American speaks Spanish, and that the numbers are the same thing.

data.question: Which statement is accurate?
choices: Fewer than 5 million people in the US speak Spanish.
About 43 million people in the US speak Spanish at home.
Every Hispanic person in the US speaks Spanish.
Spanish is spoken mainly in Florida and nowhere else in the US.

trapReasons.2: The two groups overlap a lot, so they are easy to treat as one.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: Ethnicity and language overlap but are not the same: many Hispanic Americans, especially in later generations, speak mostly English.
data.correctReasoning: The Census counts about 43 million people who speak Spanish at home; the Hispanic population (about 65 million) is a different count.
data.recoveryTip: Hispanic is about heritage; Spanish speaker is about language.

data.prompt: You see "Cuidado: piso mojado" in a store aisle. What should you do?

options.text: Watch your step: the floor is wet.

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Read the feedback and try again.

byOption.a: That would be se habla español.
byOption.b: Yes: cuidado is caution, piso is floor and mojado is wet.

blocks.purpose: Closes by turning the learner's surroundings into daily practice.

data.topic: Spanish around you in the US
data.takeaway: Tens of millions of people around you speak Spanish, and it is on your signs, your map and your TV: read it out loud every time you see it.

checks.prompt: A door sign says "Jale". What do you do?
checks.rationale: Jale means pull; push is empuje.

checks.prompt: What does the city name "Los Ángeles" mean in Spanish?
checks.rationale: Ángeles means angels, and los is the plural "the".

checks.prompt: Type the Spanish word you see on a sign that marks the way out of a building.
checks.rationale: Salida means exit; entrada is the entrance.
